title: High Throughput Proliferation and Cytotoxicity Assay for Isogenic Cell Lines
author: Ahmad, Wood, et al.
materials: Human PTEN (-/-) MCF10A Cell Line (Horizon Discovery, cat# HD 101-006)
Lentiviral construct expressing red fluorescent protein (mKate2)
IncuCyte S3 Live Cell Analysis System (Sartorius, Ann Arbor, MI)
Vi-Cell XR Cell Viability Analyzer (Beckman Coulter, Brea, CA)
D300 Digital Dispenser with T8 Cassettes (Tecan, Morrisville, NC)
Pintool head and automated liquid handling (Biomek NX, Beckman Coulter)

steps.title: Prepare 96‑well cell suspensions
steps.instruction: Adjust each PTEN KO and WT suspension to 100,000 cells · ml⁻¹ with warm media; mix equal volumes to obtain a 1:1 KO/WT mixture containing 5,000 cells in 50 µL.

steps.title: Prepare 384‑well cell suspensions
steps.instruction: Adjust each PTEN KO and WT suspension to 36,000 cells · ml⁻¹ with warm media; mix equal volumes to obtain a 1:1 KO/WT mixture containing 900 cells in 25 µL.

steps.title: Dispense media and cells (96‑well)
steps.instruction: Using a Multidrop, add 50 µL warm media to each well of a Corning 96‑well plate (Cat# 3603), then add 50 µL of the mixed cell suspension (5,000 cells) to each well for a total volume of 100 µL per well. Hand‑pipetting may be used as an alternative.

steps.title: Dispense media and cells (384‑well)
steps.instruction: Using a Multidrop, add 25 µL warm media to each well of a Corning 384‑well plate (Cat# 3764), then add 25 µL of the mixed cell suspension (900 cells) to each well for a total volume of 50 µL per well.

steps.title: Room‑temperature incubation
steps.instruction: Place the plate in the biosafety hood and incubate for 40 min at room temperature to promote even cell distribution for imaging.

steps.title: Overnight incubation at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the plate to a 37 °C incubator and incubate overnight.

steps.title: Add CellTox Green dye
steps.instruction: Dilute the CellTox Green stock 1:1000 and dispense 100 nl per well (96‑well) or 50 nl per well (384‑well) using a D300 Digital Dispenser with T8 cassettes (follow D300 instructions). Alternatively, pre‑dilute dye into media and add manually (e.g., 10 µL well⁻¹) to achieve the same final concentration.

steps.title: Add compounds and DMSO controls
steps.instruction: Using the D300 (or a Beckman NX pintool for 384‑well), add DMSO (solvent control) and test compounds dissolved in DMSO to each well at the desired concentrations. If adding manually, dilute compounds in media and add (e.g., 10 µL well⁻¹) to reach the same final concentration.

steps.title: Standardize final DMSO concentration
steps.instruction: Program the D300 to deliver compounds such that all wells, including controls, contain a final DMSO concentration of 0.1 % assay volume; the CellTox Green dye contributes an additional 0.1 % DMSO, giving a total of 0.2 % DMSO per well. Do not exceed 0.2 % DMSO unless cells are known to tolerate higher levels.

steps.title: Place plate in IncuCyte
steps.instruction: Insert the plate into the IncuCyte instrument located inside the incubator.

steps.title: Configure IncuCyte imaging schedule
steps.instruction: Using IncuCyte software 2019B rev2, create a new vessel (select Corning Cat# 3603 for 96‑well or Cat# 3764 for 384‑well), set scan type to ‘Standard’, choose adherent Cell‑by‑Cell with Phase, Red and Green channels, 10X lens, five images per well, and define a scan pattern covering all wells.

substeps.instruction: In Scan Settings, select Phase, Red, Green, 10X lens → ‘Next’.
Choose the appropriate vessel catalog number → ‘Next’.
Select wells to scan, set five images per well → ‘Next’.
Enter vessel name, cell type, date → ‘Next’.

steps.title: Run time‑course acquisition
steps.instruction: Create a schedule with scans every 6 h, stopping 3–4 days after the first scan; ensure the first scan occurs at least 40 min after plate placement in the IncuCyte and that there is a 40‑min gap before the next scan. Verify all settings and start the schedule.

steps.title: Extend total read time (optional)
steps.instruction: Schedule the total plate read time for 24 h longer than the intended experiment to allow post‑experiment extension if needed.

steps.title: Post‑experiment image gating
steps.instruction: In IncuCyte Cell‑by‑Cell software, set a red‑fluorescence gate to separate KO (high red) from WT (low red) cells based on representative low‑ and high‑red cells; set a green‑fluorescence gate to separate dead (high green) from live (low green) cells based on representative viable and dead cells.

steps.title: Calculate percent dead per population
steps.instruction: Use IncuCyte to compute % dead: for WT, (high‑green / low‑red cells) ÷ (total low‑red cells) × 100; for KO, (high‑green / high‑red cells) ÷ (total high‑red cells) × 100.

steps.title: Export data for AUC analysis
steps.instruction: For each time point, export cell counts for WT and KO and the % dead values for each well to an Excel spreadsheet.

steps.title: Perform AUC analysis in Prism
steps.instruction: Import the Excel data into GraphPad Prism; plot cell count vs time (hr) and % dead vs time for each compound concentration; calculate area under the curve (AUC) for each concentration; plot AUC of cell count vs concentration and fit a four‑parameter curve to obtain IC₅₀; plot AUC of % dead vs concentration and fit a four‑parameter curve to obtain EC₅₀.

steps.title: Endpoint analysis at selected time
steps.instruction: Choose a single time point (e.g., 48 h or 72 h), export cell counts and % dead for each well, then:

substeps.instruction: Compute relative KO proliferation: (KO cells / (KO + WT cells)) ÷ (mean of control wells’ fractions) × 100.
Compute differential KO cytotoxicity: (% dead KO) − (% dead WT).
